topics.section: Abstract; published title: Optimizing Neural Topic Modeling Pipelines for Low-Quality Speech Transcriptions

examples.question: What is Ehsan’s professional specialism?
examples.reference_answer: Ehsan is an applied AI engineer and data scientist specialising in generative and multimodal AI, open-source model adaptation and deployment, and robust AI evaluation. His experience spans policing, local government, public health and industry.

examples.question: Where did Ehsan complete his PhD, and what was his thesis about?
examples.reference_answer: He completed his PhD in Artificial Intelligence at Bournemouth University (2022–2026). His thesis is titled Deep Learning for Robust Speech Recognition and Semantic Downstream Analysis of Speech Transcriptions.

examples.question: What postgraduate qualification did Ehsan earn before his PhD?
examples.reference_answer: He earned an MSc in Data Science and Artificial Intelligence at Bournemouth University between 2019 and 2021.

examples.question: According to the supplied CV, what is Ehsan’s current role?
examples.reference_answer: The supplied CV lists him as Generative AI Engineer / KTP Associate at The Crowd Group in Poole, starting in June 2026, through a KTP with Bournemouth University supported by Innovate UK.

examples.question: How did Ehsan improve AI slide rebranding at The Crowd Group?
examples.reference_answer: He re-architected the capability in LangGraph using vision-language layout planning, deterministic validation, repair loops and raster fallback, resolving observed layout failures in regression testing.

examples.question: How is Ehsan evaluating AI-generated presentations?
examples.reference_answer: He is developing an automated evaluation framework combining deterministic scoring rubrics, LLM/VLM judges and human feedback to benchmark AI-generated presentations.

examples.question: What does Ehsan’s AI presenter prototype do?
examples.reference_answer: It narrates slides, answers audience questions and revises speaker notes. It was demonstrated as a new product capability.

examples.question: What did Ehsan deliver for Merseyside Police?
examples.reference_answer: He delivered a pipeline covering 150,000 non-emergency calls, using Whisper transcription, Llama 2 summarisation and BERTopic topic modelling. It ran on legacy CPU-only infrastructure, and its outputs informed senior-officer reports and dashboards.

examples.question: Did Ehsan need GPUs to deploy the Merseyside Police call-analysis pipeline?
examples.reference_answer: The CV says the pipeline was deployed on legacy CPU-only infrastructure after model optimisation.

examples.question: What forecasting work did Ehsan do at Surrey County Council?
examples.reference_answer: He built automated home-to-school transport demand forecasting using Prophet, benchmarked against ARIMA and ML models on three years of CRM data, to support staffing and taxi-contract planning.

examples.question: How did Ehsan replace an external EHCP planning tool?
examples.reference_answer: He built an in-house Random Forest demand-projection model with configurable population projections and a Gradio app for planners, replacing a paid third-party licence.

examples.question: What AI assurance experience does Ehsan have?
examples.reference_answer: At Surrey County Council he provided technical assurance on a government-backed RAG proof of concept, advising on evaluation, human review, prompt hardening and guardrails, and contributing to the final government report.

examples.question: How did Ehsan introduce version control at Surrey County Council?
examples.reference_answer: He secured IT approval and set up Azure DevOps for the data science team at no licence cost.

examples.question: What did Ehsan build for COVID-19 transmission surveillance?
examples.reference_answer: At Public Health Dorset he built a daily-refreshed KNIME/Python pipeline linking 15 data-warehouse tables into a pseudonymised transmission network, used during the winter 2020–21 wave.

examples.question: What were the results of Ehsan’s suspected-suicide surveillance prototype?
examples.reference_answer: The offline prototype used a 4-bit-quantised Llama 2 to identify suspected suicide attempts in free-text police records. It achieved 76% accuracy against expert labels and reduced analysis from days to minutes.

examples.question: What forecasting horizon did Ehsan provide for LiveWell Dorset?
examples.reference_answer: He built a Prophet demand forecast in Power BI that provided a one-to-two-month view of registrations for capacity planning.

examples.question: Which tools has Ehsan used to deploy open-source speech and vision-language models?
examples.reference_answer: His CV lists FastAPI, Docker, vLLM and Ollama for deployment on multi-GPU infrastructure at The Crowd Group.

examples.question: What improvements does Ehsan’s CV report for the Context-Adapter?
examples.reference_answer: The CV reports an average 24% reduction in word error rate and a 13% improvement in speech question-answering accuracy with approximately 4% extra parameters. These are reported improvements, not absolute WER or QA accuracy values.

examples.question: What problem does Ehsan’s Context-Adapter address?
examples.reference_answer: It addresses speech–LLM architectures where speech representations are computed independently of the textual prompt or contextual information is integrated uniformly. A learned gate selectively balances acoustic and contextual signals.

examples.question: Does the Context-Adapter require changing the underlying speech encoder or language decoder architecture?
examples.reference_answer: The paper describes an intermediate adapter that does not alter the architecture of the underlying encoder or decoder and is independent of the underlying speech encoder.

examples.question: Which tasks were used to evaluate the Context-Adapter?
examples.reference_answer: The study evaluates transcription and speech-based question answering, including LLM-based semantic evaluation of meaning preservation, across multiple datasets and controlled settings.

examples.question: Does the Context-Adapter simply apply more context to every speech input?
examples.reference_answer: No. It uses learned gating so that context influences acoustic representations selectively when beneficial. The paper describes selective integration rather than uniformly increasing contextual dominance.

examples.question: What factors does Ehsan’s Whisper Medium adaptation study investigate together?
examples.reference_answer: It investigates decoder adaptation depth, training-data availability and optimisation budget, comparing full-parameter fine-tuning with LoRA under data-limited and fixed-budget regimes.

examples.question: Did Ehsan’s research show that LoRA always beats full fine-tuning?
examples.reference_answer: No. LoRA captures much of the improvement using substantially fewer trainable parameters and generally retains out-of-domain performance better, but relative in-domain performance depends on the dataset and configuration.

examples.question: Can extra training on a small subset reliably replace more data in Ehsan’s Whisper study?
examples.reference_answer: No. Under fixed-budget training, repeated optimisation on small subsets does not consistently compensate for limited data. Results depend jointly on adaptation scope, data availability and optimisation regime.

examples.question: How many topic-modelling pipeline configurations did Ehsan’s published study evaluate?
examples.reference_answer: It evaluated 48 pipelines, combining four embedding models, three dimensionality-reduction choices and two clustering algorithms.

examples.question: Which components were compared in Ehsan’s topic-modelling study?
examples.reference_answer: The study compared E5, Instructor, MiniLM and SGPT embeddings; unchanged embeddings, Truncated-SVD and UMAP; and K-Means versus HDBSCAN clustering.

examples.question: What did Ehsan’s topic-modelling study find about embedding choice?
examples.reference_answer: Context-aware embeddings improved topic coherence, while larger embedding models tended to improve topic diversity. The study considered both coherence and diversity when recommending pipeline layouts.

examples.question: Are the Context-Adapter and Whisper adaptation papers already published according to the supplied CV?
examples.reference_answer: The supplied CV lists both Context-Adapter for Multimodal Speech–Language Modeling and Data and Capacity Trade-offs in In-Domain Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Whisper Medium as under review.

examples.question: Which GitHub repository accompanies Ehsan’s Whisper data-and-capacity study?
examples.reference_answer: The repository is ehsantaati/asr-scaling-depth-data. Its README describes training, evaluation, dataset preparation and statistical analysis for the Whisper-Medium adaptation study.

examples.question: Which datasets does the asr-scaling-depth-data README list for adaptation and out-of-domain evaluation?
examples.reference_answer: Adaptation uses SPGISpeech 2.0, VoxPopuli-en and GigaSpeech-M. Out-of-domain evaluation uses LibriSpeech test-clean and test-other.

examples.question: Does Ehsan’s ASR repository evaluate every decoder scope from L0 to L6?
examples.reference_answer: No. The README lists L0, L2, L3, L4, L5 and L6, and explicitly says L1 is not evaluated. The encoder is frozen in the main depth experiments.

examples.question: Does the ASR repository include the full experiment grid and completed run artifacts?
examples.reference_answer: No. The README says the examples are generic, the full experiment grid is not included, and generated run artifacts are excluded. It points to an experiment specification for the manuscript settings.

examples.question: What does Ehsan’s h2s_demand_forecast repository do?
examples.reference_answer: It forecasts Home To School Transport service demand using Prophet, converting daily records into monthly time series, tuning hyperparameters through cross-validation, and reporting MAPE and RMSE.

examples.question: Is resource allocation already complete in h2s_demand_forecast?
examples.reference_answer: The README marks resource allocation as under development; it should not be described as a completed feature.

examples.question: What is the default forecast horizon in h2s_demand_forecast, and how can I request 12 months?
examples.reference_answer: The README gives a default horizon of six months. It documents python model.py --horizon 12 for a 12-month forecast.

examples.question: Which emotions does Ehsan’s ED_Twitter project detect?
examples.reference_answer: It detects anger, fear, joy and sadness using a fine-tuned BERT model.

examples.question: How does ED_Twitter reduce bot influence and investigate emotion triggers?
examples.reference_answer: It filters bot-written tweets using a fine-tuned BERT bot detector, reported at 87% accuracy, and uses LDA topic modelling to explore themes within emotion groups for expert interpretation.

examples.question: What technologies power Ehsan’s Talking CV according to its GitHub README?
examples.reference_answer: The README describes Laravel, FastAPI and LangGraph, Qdrant retrieval with Azure OpenAI embeddings, and GitHub tools through MCP. Azure OpenAI and OpenAI are accessed through a LiteLLM gateway.

examples.question: How does Talking CV route questions to model providers?
examples.reference_answer: The README routes CV and combined CV/GitHub questions to Azure OpenAI, and GitHub or conversation questions to OpenAI. Scope and evidence checks use Azure primarily, with fallback to OpenAI.

examples.question: How does Talking CV monitor cost and latency?
examples.reference_answer: It uses LangSmith traces and dashboards to track model costs, latency and provider fallbacks.

examples.question: How does Ehsan’s transport forecasting work connect to his GitHub portfolio?
examples.reference_answer: The CV describes Prophet-based home-to-school transport demand forecasting at Surrey County Council. His h2s_demand_forecast README documents a Home To School Transport forecasting system with monthly aggregation, tuning, cross-validation, MAPE and RMSE. Together they demonstrate applied forecasting and an implementation in his portfolio.

examples.question: Give an example linking Ehsan’s public-health work with a GitHub project.
examples.reference_answer: His CV describes BERT-based public-health emotion monitoring at Public Health Dorset, rebuilt in KNIME. ED_Twitter documents the corresponding type of workflow: COVID-related tweet collection, bot filtering, four-emotion detection and LDA topic modelling in KNIME.

examples.question: wht did ehsan do with merseyside police calls?
examples.reference_answer: He delivered analysis of 150,000 non-emergency calls using Whisper transcription, Llama 2 summarisation and BERTopic topic modelling, deployed on legacy CPU-only infrastructure.
